I understand why those who bought in early at full price would be disappointed with a less than 5 hour experience. However this is far from a bad game. It is a good game for many of the reasons I really enjoyed RE2Remake, but being compared to it, it's sure to feel like a lesser experience.

It really feels like the Nemesis show ft. Jill instead of Leon and Claire ft. Mr X with how much he keeps coming back to a comical degree, and aside from the inclusion of the (debatably useful) dodge roll, it does feel like an extension to RE2Remake in areas rather than its own game. The lack of second character playthrough and bonus modes only adds to this feeling.

It is much more linear than the majority of RE2Remake and I had sooooo much gunpowder and herbs in my box at the end so healing and ammo was never an issue on standard difficulty.

If I didn't have RE4Remake, village and a bunch of other games to play in my library, I'd likely give this a second playthrough on higher difficulties, however the lack of a second character/story and the aforementioned other games means I MAY return at a later date, but for now it will be left at a <5 hour playtime.

resident evil 3 feels like everything is going wrong at once and i kind of loved that about it. the pacing was probably one of my favorite things because it never gives you too much time to settle in before something else happens. it’s stressful, chaotic, and sometimes a little ridiculous, but somehow that just adds to the fun

Another excellent remake from Capcom! I love their Resident Evil series. It's the gold standard of survival horror. This game might not be "as good" as the RE2 remake but it's pretty damn close. Looks great, plays great, and sounds great. What's not to Love? I wish it had two separate campaigns to master but hey it's still well worth a play through. Unfortunately I was far to young to play the originals back in the day so I'm willing to bet all the naysayers know more about the source material than I do. With that being said this is still a damn solid campaign story with tight game play, decent scares, and worth finishing to the end. Long live Resident Evil!

The Resident Evil 3 Remake was simply fantastic! I haven't played the original and have only played a few of the Resident Evil games, but man this game was a damn blast to complete all the achievements for.
You follow and play through the stories of Jill and Carlos during the Raccoon City outbreak. Both characters have unique game-play mechanics, while maintaining the simplistic survival horror the Resident Evil series has gotten me used to.
If you have played the Resident Evil 2 Remake, this game will feel familiar due to how the fact that it's quite similar, while adding some features such as a dodge mechanic. This game doesn't offer as much game play as the RE2 Remake, but it doesn't take away from it being fantastic. Completing all the achievements and unlocking all the infinite weapons was just incredibly addicting and fun.

9/10- The game was just an incredibly good time and has me looking forward to all future RE remakes. I cannot f*ckin wait for the RE4 Remake! I hope the that game proves to be as good as the previous couple have been.

My only complaint is the ridiculous upswing in difficulty specifically during the final Nemesis boss fight on Nightmare and Inferno. Good luck to any deathless runners- I respect you immensely.

If I could make a comparison- the RE2 remake is akin to Alien, while RE3 is more like Aliens. Both are fantastic, but for different reasons.

First things first don't listen to the hate reviews on this game. Admittedly I skipped the OG re3 game on playstation, but after playing re2 remake ( which was awesome ) I thought I'd play this game next. Resident Evil 3 is AWESOME. It pretty much picks up where re2 left off, I don't want to spoil the game for anybody who hasnt played it yet but there are some scenes included from re2 that blend into the re3 storyline which was really cool. Theres some new mechanics to this game like the ability to dodge zombie attacks, which is vital for when you have the fight scenes with nemesis. Speaking of nemesis - He just pops up out of nowhere and I found myself getting the jumpscares, almost anxious when I knew he was following me not knowing when he was going to show up. The storyline of the game is great, the characters are engaging and the maps are well laid out with your usual rezzie evil zombies plus some new creatures too. I guess the only thing missing is some boss fights like re1 and 2. Anyway I bought the game on sale and I've loved playing it, and I highly recommend to anyone thats a fan of the resident evil franchise.

Games like this are really why Steam needs a rating in-between yes and no. Resident Evil 3 Remake is a good game on its own merits, but just comes off as lazy when looking at RE2 remake, released the year prior, and RE3: Nemesis (1999).

The game on standard and hardcore is fun, albeit short, and its nice to see Jill Valentine return as a playable character in a Resident Evil game, and her movement fits the more open environments of this game compared to Leon and Claire in RE2R. Nemesis is somewhat menacing and it takes some time to understand how do deal with him, but the scare factor wears off immediately upon the realisation he can be one-shot killed with a grenade in the difficulties that matter.

RE3R removes mercenaries mode and several sections from the original, as well as the freedom of choice you're given to take your own path. The extra difficulties added to give the game extra replay value are horribly balanced in my opinion and are only somewhat enjoyable with the infinite ammo weapons. The game feels like it was made to capitalise off of the success of RE2R and I really hope Capcom doesn't cut content and really places time and effort into extra modes, preserving original content and proper balancing with RE4R.

Even on sale for $20 (at time of this review) this is a hard sell.
It has less content and less replayability than REmake 2. It's not really a good horror game like REmake 1, 2, and 7. It's not as good as an action game like 4, 5, and maybe even 6.
A fair amount of content is cut from the original game as well.
You spend most of the early game just running away from Nemesis and this system isn't done as well as Mr. X from REmake 2.

Would only recommend if you can get it really cheap (like $10) or if you're a diehard RE fan and love everything in the series.

Ladies and Gentlemen, welcome to the TL;DR edition of one of the most iconic video games in history. Im not even sure how to go about talking about this game. This game, compared to the original, is so gutted and mishandled, it should have been a DLC for Resident Evil 2 Remake. Speaking of which, how do you go from a near perfect game of RE2R to this? Was Capcom so needy of our money that they decided to give us this?

Graphics [10/10]
Sound [10/10]
Replayability [4/10]
Gameplay [4/10]
Story [3/10]
Jill Valentine [1000/10]

The only saving grace for this game (besides graphics and sound) is Jill Freakin Valentine. She is my second favorite (Claire is my number 1 <3 ). Jill is badass without being a mary sue...which is rare in todays media. If you can believe it, she was supposed to be more fleshed out than she currently is. Her PTSD from the Mansion Incident was supposed to be a major theme in this remake with the clock tower being a dream sequence. The explorable Raccoon City was originally MUCH larger, Nemesis was going to be more of a looming threat, etc.

But what we got was this.

I do recommend this game, but ONLY get it when it is on a massive sale.
